textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult. Many adolescents grow taller and notice changes in their body shape, skin, hair or voice.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult. Many adolescents grow taller and notice changes in their body shape, skin, hair or voice. Some begin having menstrual periods.
beats.speakEn: Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult. Many adolescents grow taller and notice changes in their body shape, skin, hair or voice. Some begin having menstrual periods.

beats.en: Hormones are chemical signals made in our bodies. Certain hormones help coordinate changes during puberty, along with other processes such as growth. The pituitary gland sits at the base of the brain.
beats.speakEn: Hormones are chemical signals made in our bodies. Certain hormones help coordinate changes during puberty, along with other processes such as growth. The pituitary gland sits at the base of the brain.

type: Key Concept: Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult.
Rule: Hormones are chemical signals made in our bodies.

textbookBox.concept: Eat a balanced diet with enough iron and calcium, sleep well, exercise and keep the body clean. Keeping the body and clothes clean and caring for teeth are everyday hygiene habits.

beats.en: Eat a balanced diet with enough iron and calcium, sleep well, exercise and keep the body clean. Keeping the body and clothes clean and caring for teeth are everyday hygiene habits.
beats.speakEn: Eat a balanced diet with enough iron and calcium, sleep well, exercise and keep the body clean. Keeping the body and clothes clean and caring for teeth are everyday hygiene habits.

beats.en: Mood swings, anger and worry are common in adolescence. Talking to parents, teachers or a trusted adult helps. Choose friends wisely and avoid harmful habits such as tobacco.
